assignments.text: Round 1 review: review ini.go as it is NOW against the doc comment in ini.go, case by case. Also note ini_extra_test.go exists. First line of result: OK or CHANGES: <what, precisely>.
assignments.result:
OK

Round 1 review of ini.go against its doc comment, case by case:

Sections: [name] handled by `trimmed[0]=='[' && HasSuffix(trimmed,']')`. Section name is `strings.TrimSpace` of `trimmed[1:len-1]`, case preserved. Current section pre-created as empty map on first sight, so empty sections appear (`ini_extra_test.go` line 47-49 covers it).

Empty section before any [..]: `current := ""` is the starting section; sections[""] is initialised lazily when the first key=value line is seen, so any keys before the first [header] end up under "".

Key trimming/lower-casing: `strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(trimmed[:eq]))`. Values trimmed via `strings.TrimSpace(trimmed[eq+1:])`. Map semantics give the "later key replaces earlier" rule.

Quoted values with escapes: `parseINIValue` handles both `\"` -> `"` and `\\` -> `\`. Anything else falls through and the backslash is kept literally, matching the spec which only defines those two escapes. Inner whitespace preserved (test on line 38).

Comment handling: blank lines and lines whose first non-space char is ; or # are skipped. A trailing ; or # after a value is part of the unquoted value (line 35-37 of ini_extra_test.go confirms `port = "8080 ; not a comment"`).

Error line numbers: lineNo starts at 0 and is incremented at the top of each loop iteration, so the first line is reported as "line 1". Error format is `line %d: <reason>` matching the doc.

ini_extra_test.go is consistent with the doc comment and the implementation; its error messages match the strings the implementation produces.

Tests should pass; nothing missing.

assignments.text: Round 1 review: review lru.go as it is NOW against the doc comment in lru.go, case by case. Also note lru_extra_test.go exists. First line of result: OK or CHANGES: <what, precisely>.
assignments.result:
OK

lru.go matches its doc comment on every case I checked:

- Get (lru.go:20): on hit returns (value, true) and calls touch to bump recency; on miss returns ("", false) without touching. Cap<=0 also returns miss. Correct.
- Put (lru.go:32): new key prepends to order; existing key updates value and touches (does not grow order, so eviction never spuriously fires). Eviction loop (lru.go:46) trims order and deletes the LRU map entry until len<=Cap. Correct; traced Put(a),Put(b),Put(c) at Cap=2 and confirmed a is evicted, c remains.
- Keys (lru.go:60): returns a copy of order (most->least recent); returns nil when Cap<=0 or order empty. Copy prevents aliasing. Correct.
- Len (lru.go:53): returns 0 for Cap<=0; else len(order). Correct.
- Cap<=0 (lru.go:21,33,54,61): Put is a no-op (values stays nil), Get returns ("",false), Len returns 0, Keys returns nil. Matches "holds nothing". Verified with extra test for cap 0 and -1.
- touch (lru.go:69): shifts the matched entry to index 0; verified middle (i=1) and tail (i=2) shifts are correct via copy and order[0]=key.

Traced TestLRURecencyKeysAndLen end-to-end: Put a/b/c -> [c,b,a]; Get(a) -> [a,c,b]; Put(b,22) -> [b,a,c]; Put(d) -> [d,b,a] with c evicted. All match.

lru_extra_test.go (lru_extra_test.go:1) covers recency/keys/len and Cap<=0; lru_test.go covers basic eviction and hit/miss. Tests are consistent with the doc.

No changes needed.

assignments.text: Round 1 review: review wrap.go as it is NOW (the implementer has finished; ignore any earlier look at the stub) against the doc comment in wrap.go, case by case. Also note wrap_extra_test.go exists. First line of result: OK or CHANGES: <what, precisely>.
assignments.result:
OK

Case-by-case review of wrap.go against its doc comment:

1. "Wrap breaks text into lines of at most width runes, at spaces." — Lines built by joining words with single spaces; word added only if `lineLen+1+len(runes) <= width`. Break at spaces, never mid-word. Correct.

2. "Words are separated by runs of spaces, tabs or newlines." — `strings.FieldsFunc(text, r==' '||r=='\t'||r=='\n')`. Runs collapse; no empty fields. Correct.

3. "joined on a line by single spaces." — `line += " " + w`; `lineLen += 1+len(runes)`. Correct.

4. "Word longer than width split into width-rune pieces on own lines." — When `len(runes)>width`, flush current line, then `for i:=0; i<len(runes); i+=width` emits `runes[i:min(i+width,len(runes))]`; last chunk may be shorter. Correct.

5. "Width counted in runes, not bytes." — All comparisons via `len([]rune(w))`; chunks via `string(runes[i:end])`. Multi-byte cases covered in wrap_extra_test.go. Correct.

6. "Empty or all-space text, or width<=0, gives no lines (nil)." — `width<=0` returns nil; FieldsFunc on empty/all-whitespace yields zero words → nil. Correct.

7. "Line breaks only at spaces." — Breaks at word boundaries or between split pieces of an overlong word; no mid-word breaks. Correct.

wrap_extra_test.go covers: empty, all-space, zero width, negative width, simple, collapse-whitespace, exact-fit, overlong-split, overlong-with-surrounding-words, runes (multi-byte), rune-split. All align with the doc.
